frequency_question: How often do central bank leadership teams with the intent to absorb excess liquidity actually issue and enforce an incremental reserve requirement or equivalent special ratio tool within a designated short-term window?
membership_rule: Includes any formal announcement and implementation of a temporary or incremental reserve ratio / special cash reserve mandate by a major central bank experiencing liquidity surpluses. Excludes standard permanent changes to benchmark reserve requirement ratios.

cases.name: PBoC Reserve Requirement Ratio / Special Bill deployment
Central Bank of Malaysia Additional Reserve Requirement
National Bank of Poland Additional Reserve Requirement

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 5 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 5 named major historical instances; believed to represent all clear historical instances of iCRR-type instruments in major emerging markets over the period.
known_gaps: Minor variations in smaller emerging market jurisdictions not captured.
skeleton: Targeted liquidity management tool deployments by central banks facing surplus liquidity shocks, categorized by explicit principal intent and execution capability.
multiplier: 5 hits out of 5 documented major distinct historical episodes where the intent to deploy an incremental reserve instrument was signaled and subsequently executed by the central bank principals.
validity_reason: Central bank institutional frameworks and operational toolkits for liquidity management evolve slowly over decades.
